name: GSI Helmholtzzentrum für Schwerionenforschung / FAIR
notes: FAIR (Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research) is under construction next to GSI and uses the GSI accelerators as injectors; it is recorded on this facility rather than as a separate facility because FAIR GmbH and GSI share the Darmstadt campus and management (the sources describe "GSI and FAIR" together).
The 2003 decision of the Federal Ministry of Education and Research to realise FAIR with international participation is recorded in the GSI history page.
Russian institutes' participation in FAIR experiments is suspended (statements of GSI/FAIR, 2022); not modelled.

operator_text.quote: Associates Federal Republic of Germany (90%), State of Hesse (8%), State of Rhineland-Palatinate (1%), Free State of Thuringia (1%)
operator_text.value: GSI Helmholtzzentrum für Schwerionenforschung GmbH, owned by the Federal Republic of Germany (90%), the State of Hesse (8%), Rhineland-Palatinate (1%) and Thuringia (1%); the FAIR facility is built and operated by FAIR GmbH with international partners

summary.plain: Germany's national laboratory for heavy-ion research in Darmstadt. Its UNILAC and SIS18 accelerators serve nuclear and hadron-physics experiments such as HADES, and it is building the international FAIR facility with a new 1.1 km ring, SIS100.
summary.technical: GSI Helmholtzzentrum für Schwerionenforschung GmbH (founded 1969; Helmholtz Association member; 90% Federal Republic of Germany, 8% Hesse) operating UNILAC, SIS18 and ESR, and the FAIR GmbH project building the superconducting SIS100 synchrotron, the Super-FRS, storage rings and the CBM and PANDA experiments on an adjacent site.
